stories.title: Corporate sustainability reporting requirements for 2027
stories.summary: Corporate sustainability disclosure involves laws requiring companies to report greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related financial risks. In 2027, requirements depend on company size, location, and supply chain connections. No single rule covers everyone, leaving companies to navigate a fragmented map of regional and international standards.

stories.title: UK sustainability reporting rules to impact supply chains
stories.summary: New UK sustainability reporting rules will require listed companies to track performance starting January 2027. Cambridge Marketing College notes these requirements will likely pass down through supply chains, affecting businesses beyond those directly mandated to report. Companies will report against UK Sustainability Reporting Standards on a comply or explain basis.

stories.title: Nature joins climate reporting frameworks
stories.summary: Climate-related disclosures are becoming standard for annual reports as regulators and stock exchanges increase requirements. Guidance for measuring greenhouse gas emissions across value chains has existed for two decades, and the International Sustainability Standards Board has now issued IFRS S2 to further formalize climate-related reporting.

stories.title: Canadian investors cite fiduciary duty for ESG adoption
stories.summary: A survey of Canadian investors found two-thirds consider fiduciary duty a primary driver for adopting environmental, social, and governance strategies. Despite this alignment with duty, concerns regarding the financial performance of these investments remain a factor for the surveyed group.

stories.title: SanlamAllianz publishes first sustainability report
stories.summary: Sanlam Allianz Investments Limited has published its first sustainability report, detailing ESG commitments for its KES819 billion in assets. The firm highlights a 58 percent female workforce and its integration of ESG considerations into investment decisions, ahead of new reporting requirements set to take effect in Kenya in 2027.

stories.title: FCA sets fees for ESG ratings providers
stories.summary: The Financial Conduct Authority has outlined the next phase of its plan to regulate ESG ratings providers. The regulator is establishing a framework for oversight, including the setting of regulatory fees, ahead of the official launch of the new regime.

stories.title: mobilezone Sustainability Report Receives EUPD Excellence Rating - TipRanks
Japanese firms reduce ESG-linked executive pay
stories.summary: The share of Japanese companies tying executive compensation to environmental, social, and governance targets has declined for the first time since 2021. Businesses are increasingly prioritizing investor-focused metrics like capital efficiency over ESG-based performance indicators for their leadership teams.

stories.title: Happiest Minds earns global ranking for annual report
stories.summary: Happiest Minds Technologies has secured the number 43 position in the LACP 2026 global rankings for its Integrated Annual Report, an improvement of 13 places from the previous year. The company also received a Gold award for its 2026 ESG Report in the same competition.

stories.title: MyCarbon and LDC partner on farm carbon credits
stories.summary: MyCarbon and Louis Dreyfus Company have partnered to expand a project providing technical and financial support to soybean, corn, and cotton growers in the Brazilian Savanna. The initiative aims to scale up farming practices that store carbon in the soil and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

stories.title: Nickel market faces uncertainty heading into 2027
stories.summary: The nickel market remains uncertain as high inventories and expanding production in Indonesia weigh on prices. While demand from EV batteries and stainless steel continues, recovery depends on production cuts and industrial activity. Mining companies are now looking outside Indonesia to diversify their supply chains.

stories.title: COP31: New African Development Bank report calls for climate finance that promotes peace - African Development Bank Grou
COP31 climate finance plan fails to gain support
stories.summary: An action plan proposed by Australia to ease climate finance access for vulnerable nations failed at the COP31 summit in Turkiye. Small island nations and least-developed countries declined to back the proposal, resulting in the formation of a committee to continue discussions.

stories.title: Ghana central bank pushes for carbon market investment
stories.summary: The Bank of Ghana is encouraging local financial institutions to tap into global demand for carbon market investments. The bank aims to increase participation in these markets as part of its broader strategy to leverage climate-related financial opportunities.

stories.title: KOICA grants $8.5 million for Uzbekistan carbon market
stories.summary: KOICA and the Global Green Growth Institute have signed an agreement to provide an $8.5 million grant to Uzbekistan. The project aims to establish the regulatory groundwork for trading carbon units between Uzbekistan and South Korea, including the development of guidelines and a joint action plan.

stories.title: Ardian nears target for carbon credit fund
stories.summary: Ardian has raised €230 million for its nature-based solutions investment strategy. The firm is nearing its €250 million target with backing from a group of institutional investors, as private equity firms continue to seek capital for carbon-focused vehicles.

stories.title: Ghana issues 6.5 million forest carbon credits
stories.summary: Ghana has secured 6.5 million forest carbon credits under the ART TREES standard, becoming the third country globally to do so. Buyers have committed $43 million for a portion of the credits, with the remainder potentially generating an additional $25 million in climate finance.

stories.title: First vehicle scrapping carbon credits issued in India
stories.summary: Meta Materials Circular Markets has issued 24,988 carbon credits derived from the recycling of end-of-life vehicles in India. The company provides incentives to registered scrapping facilities to encourage the use of formal recycling routes, marking the first such issuance for vehicle scrapping.

stories.title: COP31 concludes without a final agreement
stories.summary: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference ended without an overarching political agreement, the first such failure since 2009. Negotiations stalled over language regarding fossil fuels and climate finance for developing nations. The summit concluded after 50 hours of overtime, leaving the final text unsigned.

stories.title: COP31 highlights gap between climate pledges and action
stories.summary: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya served as a test for translating climate pledges into practical action. Governments faced pressure to address escalating climate risks and resource scarcity, but struggled to bridge the divide between the needs of developing countries and available climate finance.

stories.title: Antalya Pact fails to secure consensus at COP31
stories.summary: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference ended without the adoption of the Antalya Pact. After two weeks and 50 hours of extra discussions, governments failed to reach a consensus on fossil fuel transition language and climate finance. It is the first COP without an agreement since 2009.

stories.title: OPEC denies responsibility for COP31 collapse
stories.summary: OPEC Secretary General Haitham Al Ghais rejected claims that oil-producing nations were responsible for the failure of the COP31 talks. In a blog post, he stated that these countries acted in good faith and were not the parties that paralyzed negotiations or walked out.

stories.title: Australia and Turkey fail to secure COP31 pact
stories.summary: The 31st Conference of the Parties concluded without a cover decision. Australia and Turkey proposed an agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels, failing to reaffirm previous commitments. The proposal was rejected, marking the first time a COP has ended without an overarching political agreement since 2009.

stories.title: COP31 explained: Why did the UN climate summit end in deadlock? - The New Arab
COP31 Talks Collapse Without a Final Agreement - The Institute for Energy Research
Media debate follows COP31 failure
stories.summary: The collapse of COP31 has prompted global finger-pointing, with outlets blaming either oil-rich nations or European reluctance to provide climate finance. The summit ended after a coalition of nations rejected a proposed pact for its failure to mention fossil fuels. The future of the process remains questioned.

stories.title: COP31 collapse: Did the EU's methane delay undermine its fossil fuel position? - The Brussels Times
Students participate in circular economy market
stories.summary: Students at the Thames Hall Atrium attended the Anabada Circular Economy Market to swap books, clothing and electronics. The event promoted a circular economy model centered on waste elimination and material recycling. Attendees scouted sustainable vendors while a DJ provided music throughout the day.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh introduces circular economy policy
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh has become the first Indian state to launch a circular economy policy, aiming to eliminate dumping yards and process all daily waste. The state plans to establish four circular economy parks and provide investment incentives to promote recycling industries and local employment.

stories.title: Shuswap Bird of Prey and the CSRD work together to keep our landfills safe - CSRD, BC
Government funds circular economy projects
stories.summary: The government has allocated 3.4 million to support two circular economy projects focused on plastics. The initiative aims to advance material reuse and waste reduction strategies within the sector.

stories.title: Volkswagen integrates circularity into business strategy
stories.summary: Volkswagen Group has adopted a circular economy strategy, treating material reuse as a primary growth area. Chief Sustainability Officer Dirk Voeste describes the closed-loop system as both an environmental benefit and a more efficient way of doing business for the company.

stories.title: Colorado firm aims to advance coated fabric recycling through monomaterial approach - Plastics News
Expert calls for industrial waste reuse
stories.summary: An IMechE expert stated that building a circular economy based on industrial waste reuse is a national security issue due to competition for critical minerals. The institution urged the government to introduce regulations and provide investment certainty to make large-scale material recovery commercially viable.

stories.title: Volkswagen opens dismantling hub in Zwickau
stories.summary: Volkswagen has opened a new dismantling hub in Zwickau that reverses the traditional assembly line process. The facility uses an eight-station line to take end-of-life vehicles apart, aiming to turn them into recycled feedstock and used parts at industrial speed.

stories.title: Industrial park processes recycled materials in China
stories.summary: A circular economy industrial park in Fengcheng, China, is dismantling used household appliances to recover metals and plastics. These materials are processed into circuit boards and components for new products. The facility serves as a hub for local recycling enterprises.

stories.title: Bob W ties executive pay to sustainability metrics
stories.summary: Property operators often prefer marketing claims to verifiable data. Helsinki-founded Bob W links sustainability to executive compensation and publishes its emissions metrics. The company says this openness tests whether operational reality matches corporate rhetoric. Measuring footprints and funding overseas projects remains the standard for current mitigation efforts.

stories.title: BHP plans 17.4 billion dollar copper expansion in South Australia
stories.summary: BHP intends to invest 17.4 billion dollars to double its South Australian copper production by 2040. The company aims for 650,000 tonnes of annual output to supply electricity networks, renewable energy and AI infrastructure. It expects to reach 500,000 tonnes annually by 2035 before hitting its final target.

stories.title: IREDA shifts focus to asset quality over volume
stories.summary: IREDA will prioritise asset quality and prudent lending over volume-led growth as it nears 40 years of operation. Chairman Jatin Kumar Nayak said the agency will introduce clear timelines for loan processing to improve accountability. The company is currently focusing on transparency to guide its future growth strategy.

stories.title: KPI Green Energy incorporates renewable assets subsidiary
stories.summary: KPI Green Energy has incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, KP Renewable Assets Private Limited. The new entity is authorised with a subscribed capital of 100,000 rupees. As the company was incorporated on November 25, it has yet to commence business operations or report any turnover.

stories.title: Lego to build 1 billion euro factory in Portugal
stories.summary: The Lego Group plans to build a 115,000 square-meter factory in Portugal with a 1 billion euro investment. The facility is designed to source 100 percent renewable energy. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027, with the plant scheduled to open in 2030.

stories.title: Adani Energy Solutions secures 2,500 MW renewable contract
stories.summary: Adani Energy Solutions has been awarded a 2,500 MW renewable power contract. Separately, LML Realty announced the sell-out of its Jhirka Valley Industrial Park in Haryana. Over 50 companies have acquired 1.17 million square feet of space, and the developer has commenced handing over plots to buyers.

stories.title: Indian Oil targets 31 GW renewable capacity
stories.summary: Indian Oil Corporation plans to expand its renewable energy portfolio to 31 GW over the next five years. The company currently operates approximately 260 MW of capacity. It intends to invest 10,000 crore rupees annually to diversify its energy mix beyond conventional oil and gas.

stories.title: Amazon announces 7 billion dollar renewable investment in India
stories.summary: Amazon plans to invest 7 billion dollars in Indian renewable energy projects by 2030. The company unveiled four wind and solar developments with a combined capacity of 934 MW. This includes a 234 MW wind project in Karnataka, described by Amazon as its largest wind project in Asia.

stories.title: NLC India outlines 1.5 lakh crore investment plan
stories.summary: NLC India plans to invest 1.5 lakh crore rupees by 2032 to expand its renewable and thermal capacity. The state-run firm aims to increase its renewable capacity to 16 GW and thermal capacity to 15 GW. More than half of the investment is directed toward renewable energy.
